categories.main_business_segments: Apellis Pharmaceuticals operates primarily in two business segments: rare diseases and ophthalmology. Its commercial products are EMPAVELI (systemic pegcetacoplan) for paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) and SYFOVRE (intravitreal pegcetacoplan) for geographic atrophy (GA) secondary to age-related macular degeneration. The company is also developing pegcetacoplan for additional indications in hematology, nephrology, and neurology, as well as other complement-targeting therapies.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Apellis's core technology is based on the inhibition of the complement system at the level of C3, the central protein in the complement cascade. Its lead compound, pegcetacoplan, is a compstatin analog administered either systemically (subcutaneous injection) or intravitreally (eye injection). Manufacturing involves chemical synthesis, purification, and formulation, with production outsourced to third-party contract manufacturers under cGMP standards.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The primary customers are healthcare providers, hospitals, and specialty pharmacies treating patients with rare hematologic diseases (such as PNH), ophthalmologists and retina specialists treating geographic atrophy, and nephrologists and neurologists for pipeline indications. End markets include the rare disease, ophthalmology, and neurology sectors, with a focus on patients with high unmet medical needs.
categories.geographic_coverage: Apellis commercializes EMPAVELI in the United States and, through its partner Sobi, in Europe, the UK, Australia, and Saudi Arabia (as Aspaveli). SYFOVRE is approved and launched in the United States, with regulatory submissions underway in the EU, Canada, Switzerland, Australia, and the UK. The company has a global development and commercialization strategy, with a direct presence in the US and partnerships for ex-US markets.
categories.supply_chain_position: Apellis operates downstream in the supply chain, focusing on late-stage development, commercialization, and marketing of finished pharmaceutical products. It relies on third-party contract manufacturers for the production of drug substance and finished product, as well as third-party distributors and specialty pharmacies for product distribution.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The strategic focus is on expanding the clinical utility of pegcetacoplan across multiple complement-driven diseases, launching SYFOVRE for GA, and establishing EMPAVELI as a first-line treatment for PNH. R&D initiatives include developing pegcetacoplan for additional indications (ALS, C3G, IC-MPGN, CAD, HSCT-TMA), advancing new complement-targeting candidates (APL-2006, APL-1030, siRNA+EMPAVELI), and collaborating with Beam Therapeutics on gene-editing approaches.
categories.revenue_model: Apellis generates revenue primarily through product sales of EMPAVELI and SYFOVRE. Additional revenue streams include milestone payments, royalties, and development reimbursements from its collaboration with Sobi for ex-US commercialization. The company also receives upfront and milestone payments from research collaborations.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Key competitors include AstraZeneca (Soliris/eculizumab and Ultomiris/ravulizumab), Novartis (iptacopan), Iveric Bio (avacincaptad pegol), Sanofi (sutimlimab-jome), and others developing complement inhibitors or alternative therapies for PNH, GA, and related diseases. Apellis is positioned as an innovator with the first and only approved C3 inhibitor for both PNH and GA, aiming for best-in-class status and first-mover advantage in GA.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2022, Apellis had $551.8 million in cash and equivalents, generated $65.1 million in net product revenue from EMPAVELI in 2022, and reported net losses of $652.2 million for the year. The company is in a high-growth phase, transitioning from a development-stage to a commercial-stage biopharma, with significant investments in R&D and commercialization. Revenue growth is expected to accelerate with the launch of SYFOVRE and expansion of EMPAVELI.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Apellis emphasizes its unique approach of targeting C3, enabling broad inhibition of the complement system and addressing both intravascular and extravascular disease mechanisms. EMPAVELI offers self-administration and improved anemia control over C5 inhibitors in PNH, while SYFOVRE is the first and only approved treatment for GA, with demonstrated efficacy across all lesion locations and flexible dosing. The company positions its products as best-in-class, first-in-class, and addressing high unmet needs where few or no therapies exist.
